Top candidates: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt. Now viewing one reference from each.

This Sclerotinia reference matches very well - same black plastic mulch background, bleached white stem with dark sclerotia. The test image appears to be the same plant split open. Let me confirm with 3 more from other classes.

The evidence is clear:

- **Test image**: Longitudinally split stem with bleached/white interior tissue and dark hard irregular structures (sclerotia) embedded inside. Background is identical black plastic mulch.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot reference** (5593844): Same black plastic mulch background, bleached white stem with dark sclerotia — clearly from the same disease event/photo series.
- **Southern_Blight**: Shows bleached exterior but no sclerotia inside the pith; its sclerotia are small/spherical on the exterior.
- **Alternaria**: External dark canker with concentric rings, no internal sclerotia.
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Brown vascular discoloration in still-green stem — very different.

The Sclerotinia description says: "positive identification achieved by slicing the diseased stem longitudinally" — exactly what the test image shows, with the hard grayish-black sclerotia visible inside.
